experiments.name: operand dependency chain
experiments.notes: rd -> EFLAGS chain closed by x86mfflag; 1 cycle is subtracted.

latencies.notes: rd -> EFLAGS chain closed by x86mfflag; 1 cycle is subtracted. Raw measurement was 3.04; the residual is a systematic +0.03..0.1 calibration offset, so the recorded value is the nominal integer with the observed spread.

throughput.name: 8 independent lanes
throughput.asm: x86dec.d $r12; x86dec.d $r13; x86dec.d $r14; x86dec.d $r15; x86dec.d $r16; x86dec.d $r17; x86dec.d $r18; x86dec.d $r19
throughput.command: ./bench --unroll 1000 --iters 1000 --warmup 10 --reps 10 --init 'x86mtflag $r0, 1' --asm 'x86dec.d $r12; x86dec.d $r13; x86dec.d $r14; x86dec.d $r15; x86dec.d $r16; x86dec.d $r17; x86dec.d $r18; x86dec.d $r19'
throughput.notes: The instruction writes no general-purpose register, so the 8 lanes differ in their source registers and each one retires an EFLAGS write; 16.00 cycles for 8 instructions is the flag-write throughput, 2 CPI (0.5 IPC).

notes: LBT x86-style instruction. Latency is recorded for the rd accumulator path and the EFLAGS write path. Only EFLAGS is written: the general-purpose registers are read-only sources for this instruction (verified with a native test program, where every GPR keeps its value after execution while EFLAGS changes as documented, e.g. x86sub.b of 6 and 7 sets CF, SF, PF and AF).
